response.sql: WITH team_ids AS (SELECT DISTINCT team_id FROM team), team_stats AS (SELECT t.team_id, AVG(mh.w * 1.0 / NULLIF(mh.g, 0)) AS avg_win_rate, COUNT(mh.player_id) AS record_count FROM team_ids t LEFT JOIN manager_half mh ON mh.team_id = t.team_id GROUP BY t.team_id), mean_avg AS (SELECT AVG(avg_win_rate) AS mean_win_rate FROM team_stats) SELECT ts.team_id, ts.avg_win_rate, ts.record_count, ts.avg_win_rate - m.mean_win_rate AS diff_from_mean FROM team_stats ts CROSS JOIN mean_avg m WHERE m.mean_win_rate IS NOT NULL ORDER BY diff_from_mean DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A team is identified by team_id alone, so the team table's one-row-per-year entries for the same team_id are collapsed into one team; manager_half records are matched on team_id across all years.
A manager_half record with a NULL w or NULL g, or with g = 0 (which would divide by zero), contributes no win rate; these are treated as missing and excluded from the average.
w and g are multiplied by 1.0 before dividing so the win rate is fractional rather than integer-truncated.
The record count includes every manager_half row matched to the team, including rows whose win rate was excluded as missing.
The cross-team mean is the unweighted mean of the per-team averages, with teams whose average is NULL ignored; if that mean is NULL, no rows are returned.
Ties in diff_from_mean have no specified order, so which tied teams fall into the top 10 is not deterministic.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each team-season in the team table as its own team (a team is identified by year plus team_id), and match manager_half records on both year and team_id. Each output row then also shows the year.
alternatives.sql: WITH team_ids AS (SELECT DISTINCT year, team_id FROM team), team_stats AS (SELECT t.year, t.team_id, AVG(mh.w * 1.0 / NULLIF(mh.g, 0)) AS avg_win_rate, COUNT(mh.player_id) AS record_count FROM team_ids t LEFT JOIN manager_half mh ON mh.team_id = t.team_id AND mh.year = t.year GROUP BY t.year, t.team_id), mean_avg AS (SELECT AVG(avg_win_rate) AS mean_win_rate FROM team_stats) SELECT ts.year, ts.team_id, ts.avg_win_rate, ts.record_count, ts.avg_win_rate - m.mean_win_rate AS diff_from_mean FROM team_stats ts CROSS JOIN mean_avg m WHERE m.mean_win_rate IS NOT NULL ORDER BY diff_from_mean DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
